title: Chapter 3250 Take Us Back
content:
Sable kept quiet for a while, then nodded.

“The kind of world that is worth protecting. Indeed. So, then... we must conquer this Nightmare."

Sunny nodded carefully, and for a moment, his expression seemed troubled.

She looked at him, then smiled.

"You think that I'll die if the Nightmare is conquered, don't you?"

At that, Sunny was once again left unsure what to say. But since the question had already been asked, he had no choice but to answer.

With a sigh, he looked away.

"It's not certain. But there is a reason why those who challenge the Fifth Nightmare need to endure the Unmaking. It is so that they can withstand Apotheosis. If we conquer the Nightmare while you are still a mere Saint... the Spell will probably elevate your Rank to Sacred forcefully. A boy I knew became a Transcendent that way."

He looked her in the eye.

“But there is a difference between Saints and Spirits. I'm afraid... your soul might collapse if you are forced to face Apotheosis as you are now. There is no way to tell for sure."

Sable studied him in silence for a while, a soft smile playing on her lips.

Then, finishing her drink, she stood up and patted him on the shoulder.

“Still. We must conquer this Nightmare."

She headed away, then paused for a moment and added, her voice quiet:

“If it's possible... do not mention this to Nephis. She'll probably figure it out on her own, but if not... she already has enough on her plate, as it is."

With that, Sable walked away, leaving Sunny alone in the wine cellar.

He sighed and took a sip of the golden liquid — the finest wine in the Jade Palace. The wine tasted bitter.

‘It is not certain.'

Sunny did not know what would happen to Sable if they conquered the Nightmare. There was a possibility that she would perish while facing Apotheosis unprepared... but there were other possibilities, as well.

The Spell could deem her unworthy of being elevated to a higher Rank. Alternatively, it could allow her to become Sacred while bypassing Apotheosis entirely — thus making her an incomplete Spirit, someone who possessed the soul of one, but no power or authority that should go with it.

It could even make her a Spirit while replacing the missing parts with training wheels. That was what had happened to the original Sovereigns, had it not? None of them had performed an act of defiance, and yet all of them had been handed means of forming and extending their Domains.

And lastly, Sable could surprise them all and withstand Apotheosis despite her youth and inexperience. Her soul was quite special, after all.

She survived the depths of a Nightmare meant for Supremes despite entering it as a mere Master. Before that, she escaped a Cursed horror that had devastated America and reached the Seed located in a Death Zone. She even achieved natural Transcendence without anyone's help.

So who was to tell what her future held? There was no reason to expect only the worst possible outcome...

It was not like they could give up on conquering the Nightmare, regardless. Failure meant death for all of them, including Sable — so, victory was the only path to salvation.

Still, Sunny could not help but feel a new heaviness settle in his heart, adding its weight to all his other burdens.

At that moment, he was glad to have been desensitized to most emotions. He still felt them, but they did not overwhelm him as they used to... except for a few that blazed in his soul like vast, immolating flames. Nephis was one of the most scorching flames... perhaps the most scorching.

So, naturally, he was full of anticipation for the day they would be truly reunited.

Her audience with the Jade Queen came to an end. A few days later, Cassie finally recovered enough to take another Supreme Titan on a journey across ancient memories.

Just before Nephis entered her quarters, she caught the sight of Sunny leaning on a wall nearby, watching her from the shadows.

She lingered for a moment, and then spoke in an even, emotionless tone:

"Do you hope that I will be changed after walking through this door?"

Sunny lingered for a moment, then nodded silently.

Nephis turned away, facing the door, and smiled faintly.

“I met War God once, you know."

Sunny raised an eyebrow.

“You did?"

Nephis inhaled deeply, then slowly exhaled.

“Yes. She told me a lot of things... about change, among other things. She also said that they chose a path and followed it to the end earnestly. She said that I had lost my way."

Neph's smile disappeared slowly.

“She told me that they could not win the war... because they loved the daemons. How foolish."

She tilted her head a little, remained silent for a short while, and then spoke in a neutral tone:

"But I do not love anything — or anyone. Love is not something I am capable of... have been capable for a long, long time."

She inhaled deeply.

"So, it seems that I have a long way to go before becoming a god."

Sunny studied her without saying anything, taken aback by her words.

‘Because they... loved the daemons?'

The thought was so preposterous, so ill-fitting. So against everything he had known, or at least believed that he had known.

But it also carried an overwhelming, unmistakable scent of truth.

'What does it mean?'

Eventually, Nephis spoke evenly:

“She also promised to kill me the next time we meet."

Sunny flinched, forgetting all about his thoughts.

"What?"

War God had promised to kill Nephis? Suddenly, a sense of insurmountable dread grasped his heart with icy claws, paralyzing him.

Nephis smiled coldly.

"She had a very high opinion of herself, that old goddess. Who says that I won't kill her, instead?"

Chuckling with a hint of self-mockery, she raised her hand and placed it on the door handle.

"Still. If I am to face her again, shouldn't I at least try to become a bit more like a god?"

With that, she opened the door and walked inside.

A moment later, the door closed, leaving Sunny alone in the corridor.

Rattled, uneasy.

Full of grim wariness and powerless anger. Eventually, exhaling heavily, he looked down and clenched his fists.

"...You should. And I, as well."
